q.hi: Interviewer bolta hai "Design WhatsApp". Pehle ~5 min me sabse sahi kaam kya hai?
q.en: The interviewer says "Design WhatsApp". What is the best thing to do in the first ~5 minutes?

hi: Functional + non-functional requirements clarify karna aur out-of-scope likhna
Detailed capacity estimation 10 min tak karna
Seedha LB, Kafka, Cassandra wala diagram banana
Saare tables ka full schema columns ke saath likhna
en: Clarify functional + non-functional requirements and note what is out of scope
Spend 10 minutes on detailed capacity estimation
Jump straight to a diagram with LB, Kafka and Cassandra
Write the full schema of every table with all columns

why.hi: Requirements step me scope aur NFR (scale, latency, consistency) fix hote hain. Bina iske galat problem solve hoti hai, jaise group chat scope me tha hi nahi.
why.en: The requirements step fixes scope and NFRs (scale, latency, consistency). Skipping it means solving the wrong problem, e.g. building group chat that was never in scope.

q.hi: HLD round me capacity estimation kab karni chahiye?
q.en: When should you do capacity estimation in an HLD round?

hi: Hamesha shuru me 10 min detailed math, bandwidth se cache size tak
Sirf jab number koi design decision badle, jaise "1M QPS reads hai, cache zaroori hai"
Kabhi nahi, interviewer numbers nahi dekhta
Sirf wrap-up me, design khatam hone ke baad
en: Always up front, 10 minutes of detailed math from bandwidth to cache size
Only when a number changes a design decision, e.g. "1M QPS of reads, so a cache is needed"
Never, interviewers do not care about numbers
Only during wrap-up, after the design is done

why.hi: Framework kehta hai sirf woh number nikalo jo decision badle. 10 min ki math deep dive ka time kha jaati hai.
why.en: The framework says compute only numbers that change a decision. Ten minutes of math eats the deep-dive time.

q.hi: Senior (SDE-3+) candidate ka sabse bada signal kya hai?
q.en: What is the strongest signal of a senior (SDE-3+) candidate?

hi: Zyada se zyada technologies ke naam lena
Shuru se hi sharding aur multi-region design karna
Interviewer ke poochne se pehle khud batana ki kya toot sakta hai (bottlenecks, failure modes)
Diagram sabse jaldi complete karke chup ho jaana
en: Naming as many technologies as possible
Designing sharding and multi-region from the very start
Proactively saying what can break (bottlenecks, failure modes) before the interviewer asks
Finishing the diagram fastest and then going quiet

why.hi: Senior se expectation hai ki interviewer ko kam bolna pade: failure modes, consistency choices, cost khud uthao.
why.en: Seniors are expected to drive: raise failure modes, consistency choices and cost without being asked.

q.hi: WhatsApp ke long-lived WebSocket connections ke liye kaunsa LB algorithm better hai?
q.en: Which LB algorithm suits WhatsApp's long-lived WebSocket connections best?

hi: Round robin
Weighted round robin
Random selection
Least connections
en: Round robin
Weighted round robin
Random selection
Least connections

why.hi: Long-lived connections me har server pe active connections alag hote hain. Least connections kam load wale server ko bhejta hai, round robin nahi dekhta.
why.en: With long-lived connections, active counts differ per server. Least connections routes to the least-loaded one; round robin ignores load.

q.hi: IPL ke liye Hotstar ne app tier 20 se 300 servers kar diya. Sabse pehle kya toot sakta hai?
q.en: For IPL, Hotstar scaled the app tier from 20 to 300 servers. What is likely to break first?

hi: DB connections khatam ho jaana, isliye connection pooling (PgBouncer) chahiye
L7 LB HTTP parse nahi kar paayega
JWT tokens naye servers pe invalid ho jaayenge
Stateless servers ke beech session mismatch ho jayega
en: The DB runs out of connections, so connection pooling (PgBouncer) is needed
The L7 LB will no longer be able to parse HTTP
JWT tokens become invalid on the new servers
Sessions will mismatch between the stateless servers

why.hi: App tier aasani se scale hota hai, DB nahi. Har server ka connection pool DB pe connections phula deta hai.
why.en: The app tier scales easily but the DB does not. Each server's pool multiplies connections on the DB.

q.hi: Sticky sessions ko default kyun nahi banana chahiye?
q.en: Why should sticky sessions not be the default?

hi: Sticky sessions L7 load balancer pe support hi nahi hote
Server mara to uske users ka session gaya, aur load uneven hota hai
Sticky sessions se har request pe ek extra DB write hota hai
Sticky sessions JWT ko invalid kar dete hain
en: Sticky sessions are not supported on L7 load balancers
If a server dies its users lose their sessions, and load becomes uneven
Sticky sessions add an extra DB write on every request
Sticky sessions invalidate JWTs

why.hi: Default: stateless servers, JWT for auth + Redis for session state. Sticky me state ek server se bandh jaati hai.
why.en: Default: stateless servers, JWT for auth + Redis for session state. Sticky sessions tie state to one server.

q.hi: Paytm wallet ka balance aur transactions store karne ke liye best choice?
q.en: Best choice to store Paytm wallet balance and transactions?

hi: Cassandra, kyunki write-heavy hai
MongoDB, kyunki schema flexible hai
Postgres / MySQL, kyunki ACID aur multi-row transactions chahiye
Redis, kyunki sub-ms latency hai
en: Cassandra, because it is write-heavy
MongoDB, because the schema is flexible
Postgres / MySQL, because ACID and multi-row transactions are needed
Redis, because it has sub-ms latency

why.hi: Paise wale data me eventual consistency galti hai. ACID, unique constraints aur transactions ke liye SQL.
why.en: Eventual consistency is a mistake for money. SQL gives ACID, unique constraints and transactions.

q.hi: Cassandra table: messages(chat_id, message_ts, ..., PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, message_ts)). Yahan chat_id ka role kya hai?
q.en: Cassandra table: messages(chat_id, message_ts, ..., PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, message_ts)). What is the role of chat_id?

hi: Clustering key: rows ko sort karta hai, aur message_ts node decide karta hai
Secondary index jo ad-hoc joins enable karta hai
Sirf ek UNIQUE constraint, data placement pe koi asar nahi
Partition key: decide karta hai data kis node pe jaayega; message_ts us partition me sort karta hai
en: Clustering key: sorts rows, while message_ts decides the node
A secondary index that enables ad-hoc joins
Just a UNIQUE constraint with no effect on placement
Partition key: decides which node holds the data; message_ts sorts rows inside that partition

why.hi: Ek chat ke saare messages ek partition me time order me, isliye "last 50 messages" ek fast range read hai.
why.en: All messages of one chat live in one partition in time order, so "last 50 messages" is a fast range read.

q.hi: Candidate bolta hai: "Movie bookings ke liye NoSQL lunga kyunki scale hoga." Load ~100 writes/sec hai. Best critique?
q.en: A candidate says: "I will use NoSQL for movie bookings because it scales." Load is ~100 writes/sec. Best critique?

hi: Bina numbers ka justification hai; 100 writes/sec aur UNIQUE/ACID need ke liye Postgres kaafi aur better hai
Bookings ke liye Neo4j lena chahiye tha
Elasticsearch ko primary DB banana chahiye tha
Redis ko bina persistence ke primary store bana do
en: It is justified without numbers; at 100 writes/sec with UNIQUE/ACID needs, Postgres is enough and better
Neo4j should have been chosen for bookings
Elasticsearch should be the primary DB
Use Redis as the primary store without persistence

why.hi: DB choice access pattern, consistency need aur scale numbers se justify karo. Tuned Postgres ~10K+ writes/sec le leta hai.
why.en: Justify DB choice with access pattern, consistency need and scale numbers. A tuned Postgres handles ~10K+ writes/sec.

q.hi: Swiggy orders table pe INDEX (user_id, created_at) hai. Kaunsi query is index ko use NAHI kar paayegi?
q.en: Swiggy's orders table has INDEX (user_id, created_at). Which query can NOT use this index?

hi: WHERE user_id = 5
WHERE created_at > '2026-01-01'
WHERE user_id = 5 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10
WHERE user_id = 5 AND created_at > '2026-01-01'
en: WHERE user_id = 5
WHERE created_at > '2026-01-01'
WHERE user_id = 5 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10
WHERE user_id = 5 AND created_at > '2026-01-01'

why.hi: Leftmost prefix rule: composite index pehle user_id se sorted hai. user_id ke bina sirf created_at pe filter index use nahi karta.
why.en: Leftmost prefix rule: the composite index is sorted by user_id first. Filtering only on created_at cannot use it.

q.hi: User ne profile photo badli, refresh kiya, aur purani photo dikhi (read async replica se gaya). Sahi fix?
q.en: A user changed their profile photo, refreshed, and saw the old one (the read hit an async replica). Right fix?

hi: Aur read replicas add karo
Profile table ka index hata do
Read-your-writes: jisne last ~10 sec me likha, uski reads leader se karo
Multi-leader replication pe shift karo
en: Add more read replicas
Drop the index on the profile table
Read-your-writes: route reads to the leader for users who wrote in the last ~10 seconds
Switch to multi-leader replication

why.hi: Async replication me lag ms se seconds tak hota hai. Replicas badhane se lag nahi jaata; recent writer ko leader se padhao.
why.en: Async replication lags by ms to seconds. More replicas do not remove lag; serve recent writers from the leader.

q.hi: Failover ke baad purana leader wapas aaya aur khud ko leader samajh ke writes lene laga. Ise kya kehte hain aur fix kya hai?
q.en: After failover the old leader came back and kept accepting writes as leader. What is this, and the fix?

hi: Replication lag; read-your-writes se fix
Hot partition; key salting se fix
Cache stampede; request coalescing se fix
Split brain; fencing token / epoch number aur consensus (Raft, etcd, ZooKeeper) se rokna
en: Replication lag; fix with read-your-writes
Hot partition; fix with key salting
Cache stampede; fix with request coalescing
Split brain; prevent it with fencing tokens / epoch numbers and consensus (Raft, etcd, ZooKeeper)

why.hi: Do leaders = conflicting writes. Epoch/fencing token se purane leader ke writes reject hote hain.
why.en: Two leaders means conflicting writes. Epoch/fencing tokens make the stale leader's writes get rejected.

q.hi: Swiggy orders ko shard karna hai aur main query "mere orders" hai. Best shard key?
q.en: You must shard Swiggy orders and the main query is "my orders". Best shard key?

hi: user_id
country
order status
order date (range sharding)
en: user_id
country
order status
order date (range sharding)

why.hi: user_id high cardinality hai aur main query ek hi shard pe jaati hai. country/status low cardinality, date se aaj ka shard hot.
why.en: user_id has high cardinality and keeps the main query on one shard. country/status are low cardinality; date makes today's shard hot.

q.hi: shard = hash(key) % N use ho raha hai. N ko 8 se 9 kiya. Kya hoga?
q.en: You use shard = hash(key) % N and change N from 8 to 9. What happens?

hi: Sirf ~1/9 data move hoga
Lagbhag saara data reshuffle hoga; consistent hashing me sirf ~1/N move hota
Koi data move nahi hoga, sirf naye writes naye shard pe jaayenge
Sirf range queries toot jaayengi, data wahi rahega
en: Only ~1/9 of the data moves
Almost all data gets reshuffled; with consistent hashing only ~1/N would move
No data moves; only new writes go to the new shard
Only range queries break; data stays put

why.hi: Modulo badalne pe almost har key ka shard badal jaata hai. Isliye fixed logical shards ya consistent hashing.
why.en: Changing the modulus remaps almost every key. Hence fixed logical shards or consistent hashing.

q.hi: Consistent hashing ring pe virtual nodes (har server 100-200 jagah) ka main fayda kya hai?
q.en: What is the main benefit of virtual nodes (each server at 100-200 ring positions) in consistent hashing?

hi: Range queries ek hi node pe chalne lagti hain
Cross-shard transactions possible ho jaate hain
Load even hota hai, aur node mare to uska load sab nodes me batta hai, sirf ek padosi pe nahi
Replication ki zarurat khatam ho jaati hai
en: Range queries start running on a single node
Cross-shard transactions become possible
Load evens out, and a dead node's load spreads across all nodes instead of one neighbour
Replication is no longer needed

why.hi: Bina vnodes ke ek node ko bada arc mil sakta hai. Vnodes se bade server ko zyada vnodes bhi de sakte ho.
why.en: Without vnodes one node may own a huge arc. Vnodes also let bigger servers take more positions.

q.hi: Cache-aside pattern me Zomato menu update hua. Write path pe sahi order kya hai?
q.en: With cache-aside, a Zomato menu is updated. What is the right write-path order?

hi: Pehle cache update, phir DB update
Sirf cache me likho, DB baad me batch me
DB update, phir cache me naya value SET karo
Pehle DB update, phir cache key DELETE
en: Update the cache first, then the DB
Write only to cache, flush to DB later in batches
Update the DB, then SET the new value in the cache
Update the DB first, then DELETE the cache key

why.hi: Update ke bajaye delete karne se race me stale value likhne ka chance kam hota hai. Agli read DB se fresh laayegi.
why.en: Deleting instead of updating reduces the chance of a race writing a stale value. The next read refills fresh data.

q.hi: IPL score ki popular key expire hui aur ek saath 10,000 requests DB pe gir gayi. Best fix?
q.en: A popular IPL score key expired and 10,000 requests hit the DB at once. Best fix?

hi: Request coalescing (single flight) + TTL jitter / early refresh
Saari keys ka same lamba TTL rakh do
Eviction LRU se LFU kar do
Redis hata ke Memcached laga do
en: Request coalescing (single flight) + TTL jitter / early refresh
Give every key the same long TTL
Switch eviction from LRU to LFU
Replace Redis with Memcached

why.hi: Ye cache stampede hai. Sirf ek request DB jaaye, baaki wait karein; jitter se keys ek saath expire nahi hoti.
why.en: This is a cache stampede. Let one request hit the DB while others wait; jitter stops keys expiring together.

q.hi: Instagram likes/view counts ke liye kaunsa caching pattern sabse fit hai (thoda data loss chalega, writes bahut fast chahiye)?
q.en: Which caching pattern best fits Instagram like/view counts (small loss is OK, writes must be very fast)?

hi: Write-through
Write-back (write-behind)
Write-around
Cache-aside with delete on every write
en: Write-through
Write-back (write-behind)
Write-around
Cache-aside with delete on every write

why.hi: Write-back me write sirf cache me jaata hai aur DB me batch me. Counters ke liye perfect; cache mara to thoda loss.
why.en: Write-back writes only to cache and flushes to DB in batches. Ideal for counters; a cache crash loses a little.

q.hi: Candidate bolta hai "Hum CA system banayenge". Ye kyun galat hai?
q.en: A candidate says "We will build a CA system". Why is this wrong?

hi: CA systems sirf NoSQL me milte hain
CA ka matlab hai ACID consistency, jo distributed me impossible hai
Distributed system me partition hota hi hai, P mandatory hai; asli choice partition ke time C ya A hai
CA systems hamesha slow hote hain, PACELC ke hisaab se
en: CA systems only exist in NoSQL
CA means ACID consistency, which is impossible when distributed
Partitions happen in any distributed system, so P is mandatory; the real choice is C or A during a partition
CA systems are always slow according to PACELC

why.hi: Network partition real life me hota hai. CAP ka C aur ACID ka C bhi alag cheezein hain.
why.en: Network partitions happen in real life. Also, CAP's C and ACID's C are different things.

q.hi: Cassandra me N=3 replicas. Kaunsa setting quorum consistency deta hai (R + W > N)?
q.en: Cassandra with N=3 replicas. Which setting gives quorum consistency (R + W > N)?

why.hi: 2+2=4 > 3, to read aur write sets overlap karte hain aur latest value milti hai. Baaki options me sum 3 ya kam hai.
why.en: 2+2=4 > 3, so read and write sets overlap and the latest value is found. The others sum to 3 or less.

q.hi: BookMyShow me consistency kaise choose karoge?
q.en: How would you choose consistency for BookMyShow?

hi: Per feature: search/browse eventual (AP), booking path strong (CP)
Poora system strong consistency, search bhi
Poora system eventual, double booking baad me refund se theek
Booking eventual, search strong
en: Per feature: search/browse eventual (AP), booking path strong (CP)
Strong consistency for the whole system, including search
Eventual everywhere; fix double bookings later with refunds
Eventual for booking, strong for search

why.hi: Double booking ka cost downtime se zyada hai, par search thoda stale chalega. Ek system me alag features alag level.
why.en: Double booking costs more than downtime, but slightly stale search is fine. Different features get different levels.

q.hi: Kafka me message ordering kahan tak guaranteed hai?
q.en: How far does Kafka guarantee message ordering?

hi: Poore topic me
Sirf ek partition ke andar
Poore cluster me saare topics ke beech
Sirf ek consumer group ke andar, partitions se farak nahi
en: Across the whole topic
Only within a single partition
Across all topics in the cluster
Within one consumer group, regardless of partitions

why.hi: Isliye chat me key = chat_id, payments me key = account_id rakhte hain, taaki ek entity ke events ek partition me order me rahein.
why.en: That is why chat uses key = chat_id and payments key = account_id, keeping one entity's events ordered in one partition.

q.hi: Swiggy ke orders topic me 12 partitions hain. Notification consumer group me 20 consumers chala diye. Kya hoga?
q.en: Swiggy's orders topic has 12 partitions. You run 20 consumers in the notification consumer group. What happens?

hi: Saare 20 consumers load share karenge
Har message 20 baar process hoga
12 consumers kaam karenge, 8 idle baithenge
Kafka automatically 20 partitions bana dega
en: All 20 consumers share the load
Every message is processed 20 times
12 consumers work and 8 sit idle
Kafka automatically creates 20 partitions

why.hi: Ek group me har partition sirf ek consumer ko milta hai. Isliye partitions pehle se kaafi (50-100) rakho.
why.en: Within a group each partition goes to only one consumer. So provision enough partitions (50-100) up front.

q.hi: Ek kharab "poison message" baar baar fail ho raha hai aur poori partition atak gayi. Sahi fix?
q.en: A bad "poison message" keeps failing and blocks the whole partition. Right fix?

hi: Offset pehle commit karo (at-most-once) taaki message skip ho
Retention 7 din se 30 din kar do
Consumer group me aur consumers add karo
3-5 retries (backoff ke saath) ke baad message DLQ me daalo, alert lagao
en: Commit the offset first (at-most-once) so the message is skipped
Increase retention from 7 to 30 days
Add more consumers to the group
After 3-5 retries with backoff, move it to a DLQ and alert

why.hi: DLQ se ek bad message partition block nahi karta. At-most-once se baaki messages bhi kho sakte hain.
why.en: A DLQ keeps one bad message from blocking the partition. At-most-once risks losing other messages too.

q.hi: LLM chat app me response tokens stream karne hain (sirf server se client). Sabse simple sahi choice?
q.en: An LLM chat app streams response tokens (server to client only). Simplest correct choice?

hi: SSE (Server-Sent Events)
WebSocket
Short polling har 1 sec
Long polling
en: SSE (Server-Sent Events)
WebSocket
Short polling every 1 sec
Long polling

why.hi: One-way push ke liye SSE kaafi hai: normal HTTP, auto-reconnect built-in. WebSocket ki complexity nahi chahiye.
why.en: SSE is enough for one-way push: plain HTTP with built-in auto-reconnect. No need for WebSocket complexity.

q.hi: 10M concurrent users ke WebSocket connections hain, ek gateway safely ~100K connections leta hai. Kitne gateway servers chahiye?
q.en: There are 10M concurrent WebSocket users and one gateway safely holds ~100K connections. How many gateway servers?

why.hi: 10M / 100K = 100. Tuned box 1M tak ja sakta hai, par interview me 100K safe bolo.
why.en: 10M / 100K = 100. A tuned box can reach 1M, but say 100K as the safe number in interviews.

q.hi: Rahul ka message Redis Pub/Sub se Priya ke gateway ko bheja, par us waqt woh gateway restart ho raha tha aur message kho gaya. Root cause aur fix?
q.en: Rahul's message was published via Redis Pub/Sub to Priya's gateway, but that gateway was restarting and the message was lost. Root cause and fix?

hi: L7 LB use karo, L4 ki jagah
Presence TTL 60 sec se badha ke 10 min karo
Pub/Sub fire-and-forget hai; message pehle DB me persist karo, reconnect pe client last_seen_msg_id se sync kare
WebSocket hata ke long polling lagao
en: Use an L7 LB instead of L4
Raise the presence TTL from 60 sec to 10 min
Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget; persist the message to the DB first and sync on reconnect using last_seen_msg_id
Replace WebSocket with long polling

why.hi: Redis Pub/Sub durable nahi hai; subscriber down tha to message gaya. Offline user ko DB + push notification se milta hai.
why.en: Redis Pub/Sub is not durable; if the subscriber is down the message is gone. Offline users get it from the DB + push.

q.hi: SET seat:A5 rahul NX PX 600000 me NX kya karta hai?
q.en: In SET seat:A5 rahul NX PX 600000, what does NX do?

hi: Key ko 600 sec ke liye expire karta hai
Key ko disk pe persist karta hai
Purani value overwrite karke naya owner set karta hai
Key tabhi set hogi jab pehle se exist na kare, isse atomic check-and-set milta hai
en: Expires the key after 600 seconds
Persists the key to disk
Overwrites the old value and sets a new owner
Sets the key only if it does not already exist, giving an atomic check-and-set

why.hi: NX = "not exists". PX 600000 alag hai, woh 10 min ka TTL deta hai taaki payment chhodne pe seat free ho.
why.en: NX means "not exists". PX 600000 is separate: a 10-min TTL so the seat frees up if payment is abandoned.

q.hi: Seat hold ke liye Redis lock hai. Phir bhi bookings table pe UNIQUE(show_id, seat_id) kyun rakho?
q.en: Seat holds use a Redis lock. Why still keep UNIQUE(show_id, seat_id) on the bookings table?

hi: Defense in depth: Redis down ho ya lock kho jaye tab bhi DB double booking rokega
UNIQUE constraint se Redis lock fast ho jaata hai
Redis lock ka TTL DB constraint se set hota hai
UNIQUE constraint seat ko 10 min hold karta hai
en: Defense in depth: if Redis fails or a lock is lost, the DB still prevents double booking
The UNIQUE constraint makes the Redis lock faster
The Redis lock TTL is derived from the DB constraint
The UNIQUE constraint holds the seat for 10 minutes

why.hi: Sirf Redis lock pe bharosa common galti hai. Constraint hold nahi karta, par last line of defense hai.
why.en: Relying only on a Redis lock is a common mistake. The constraint does not hold seats but is the last line of defense.

q.hi: Ek design me seat ko SELECT ... FOR UPDATE se lock karke user ke 10 min payment tak transaction khula rakha. Kya fail hoga?
q.en: A design locks the seat with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and keeps the transaction open for the user's 10-min payment. What fails?

hi: Optimistic locking ki tarah bahut retries honge
Locks aur DB connections lambe time tak pakde rahenge, connections khatam aur deadlock ka risk
Do users ko same seat mil jayegi
Redis lock ka TTL expire ho jayega
en: There will be many retries, like optimistic locking
Locks and DB connections are held for minutes, exhausting connections and risking deadlocks
Two users will get the same seat
The Redis lock TTL will expire

why.hi: Pessimistic lock chhote transactions ke liye hai. Lambe hold ke liye Redis lock with TTL, final booking DB constraint ke saath.
why.en: Pessimistic locks suit short transactions. For long holds use a Redis lock with TTL and a DB constraint for the final booking.

q.hi: Paytm "Pay" API ke liye Idempotency-Key kaun generate kare?
q.en: Who should generate the Idempotency-Key for Paytm's "Pay" API?

hi: Server, har incoming request pe naya UUID
Database, auto-increment ID se
Client, har logical operation ke liye ek, aur retry pe wahi key
Load balancer, request hash se
en: The server, a new UUID per incoming request
The database, from an auto-increment ID
The client, one per logical operation, reusing the same key on retry
The load balancer, from a request hash

why.hi: Server pe banegi to retry pe nayi key milegi aur dedup fail. Client ki key retry pe same rehti hai.
why.en: If the server generates it, a retry gets a new key and dedup fails. The client's key stays the same on retry.

q.hi: Client → API → Service → DB, aur teeno layers har failure pe 3 retry karti hain. Worst case me DB pe load kitna guna ho sakta hai?
q.en: Client → API → Service → DB, and all three layers retry 3 times on failure. Worst case, how many times the load can the DB see?

why.hi: 3 x 3 x 3 = 27. Isliye retry sirf ek layer pe, retry budget, circuit breaker aur backoff + jitter.
why.en: 3 x 3 x 3 = 27. So retry at one layer only, with a retry budget, circuit breaker and backoff + jitter.

q.hi: Idempotency key ko dedup table me insert karna aur debit karna, dono kaise karne chahiye?
q.en: How should inserting the idempotency key into the dedup table and doing the debit be done?

hi: Ek hi DB transaction me, key pe PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE constraint ke saath
Pehle debit commit, phir alag transaction me key insert
Key sirf Redis me SET NX, DB me kuch nahi
Key ko Kafka me publish karo, consumer baad me debit kare
en: In one DB transaction, with a PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE constraint on the key
Commit the debit first, then insert the key in a separate transaction
Store the key only in Redis with SET NX, nothing in the DB
Publish the key to Kafka and let a consumer debit later

why.hi: Alag transactions me beech ka crash adhuri state chhodta hai (debit hua par key nahi, retry pe double charge). Redis fast path hai, source of truth DB.
why.en: Separate transactions leave half-done state on a crash (debited but no key, so a retry double-charges). Redis is a fast path; the DB is the source of truth.

q.hi: Sliding window counter, limit 100/min. 10:01:15 pe current window me 30 requests, previous window me 80. Estimated count?
q.en: Sliding window counter, limit 100/min. At 10:01:15 the current window has 30 requests and the previous one had 80. Estimated count?

hi: 30 (sirf current window)
en: 30 (current window only)

why.hi: 15 sec current window me gaye, to previous window ka 75% abhi bhi 60 sec ke andar overlap karta hai.
why.en: 15 seconds into the current window, 75% of the previous window still overlaps the last 60 seconds.

q.hi: IRCTC ke 10 gateway servers har ek apni local memory me counter rakhte hain, limit 100/min per user. Kya galat hai?
q.en: IRCTC's 10 gateway servers each keep a counter in local memory, limit 100/min per user. What is wrong?

hi: Kuch nahi, LB requests evenly baant deta hai to limit sahi rahegi
Limit 10/min ho jayegi
Effective limit ~1000/min ho jaati hai; counter central Redis me (Lua se atomic) rakho
Sirf fixed window ki boundary burst problem aayegi
en: Nothing, the LB spreads requests evenly so the limit stays correct
The limit drops to 10/min
The effective limit becomes ~1000/min; keep the counter in central Redis (atomic via Lua)
Only the fixed-window boundary burst problem appears

why.hi: Distributed setup me local counters limit ko servers ki ginti se multiply kar dete hain.
why.en: In a distributed setup, local counters multiply the limit by the number of servers.

q.hi: Rate limiter ka Redis down ho gaya. Generally kya karna chahiye?
q.en: The rate limiter's Redis is down. What should generally happen?

hi: Sab endpoints pe fail closed, sabko 429
Sab endpoints pe fail open, OTP pe bhi
Har gateway local counter pe switch kare aur limit 10x kar de
Fail open (requests allow), par OTP/payment jaise sensitive endpoints pe fail closed
en: Fail closed everywhere, return 429 to everyone
Fail open everywhere, including OTP
Each gateway switches to a local counter and raises the limit 10x
Fail open (allow requests), but fail closed on sensitive endpoints like OTP/payment

why.hi: Limiter ki wajah se poori site girna nahi chahiye, par abuse-prone sensitive endpoints ko bachao.
why.en: The limiter should not take down the whole site, but protect abuse-prone sensitive endpoints.

q.hi: Dropbox pe user 2 GB file upload kar raha hai. Best upload path?
q.en: A Dropbox user uploads a 2 GB file. Best upload path?

hi: Server auth check karke pre-signed URL de, client seedha S3 pe (multipart) upload kare
File app server pe aaye, server S3 pe forward kare
File DB ke BLOB column me store karo
File Kafka topic me bhejo, consumer S3 me likhe
en: Server checks auth and returns a pre-signed URL; client uploads directly to S3 (multipart)
File goes to the app server, which forwards it to S3
Store the file in a DB BLOB column
Send the file into a Kafka topic and let a consumer write to S3

why.hi: App server ke through proxy karna bandwidth aur memory waste hai. Rule: metadata DB me, bytes S3 me.
why.en: Proxying through the app server wastes bandwidth and memory. Rule: metadata in the DB, bytes in S3.

q.hi: YouTube upload API ke andar hi synchronous transcoding (240p se 4K) kar di. Kya fail hoga?
q.en: A YouTube upload API does transcoding (240p to 4K) synchronously inside the request. What fails?

hi: CDN cache miss badh jaayenge
Transcoding minutes leti hai, request timeout hogi aur retry pe kaam double; queue + async workers chahiye
HLS manifest generate hi nahi ho sakta
S3 durability 11 nines se kam ho jayegi
en: CDN cache misses will increase
Transcoding takes minutes, so requests time out and retries duplicate work; it needs a queue + async workers
The HLS manifest cannot be generated at all
S3 durability drops below 11 nines

why.hi: CPU-heavy lamba kaam hamesha async: queue, parallel workers, aur 202 + status.
why.en: CPU-heavy long work is always async: a queue, parallel workers, and 202 + status.

q.hi: App ki JS/CSS CDN pe hai. Naya release deploy hua. Cache invalidation ka best tareeka?
q.en: App JS/CSS sits on a CDN and a new release ships. Best way to handle cache invalidation?

hi: Har deploy pe Purge API se poora cache saaf karo
TTL 0 rakh do taaki CDN kabhi cache na kare
Versioned URLs (app.a8f3c.js), content badla to naya URL
Push CDN pe shift karo taaki invalidation ki zarurat na pade
en: Purge the whole cache via the Purge API on every deploy
Set TTL to 0 so the CDN never caches
Versioned URLs (app.a8f3c.js), so changed content gets a new URL
Move to a push CDN so invalidation is never needed

why.hi: Purge slow aur mehenga hai, sirf galti sudharne ke liye. Versioned URL se purana apne TTL se mar jaata hai.
why.en: Purge is slow and costly, meant for fixing mistakes. With versioned URLs the old file simply ages out by TTL.

q.hi: Bangalore me 50,000 drivers online hain, har driver har 4 sec location bhejta hai. Approx writes/sec?
q.en: Bangalore has 50,000 online drivers, each sending location every 4 sec. Approximate writes/sec?

hi: ~200K writes/sec
~1.25K writes/sec
~50K writes/sec
~12.5K writes/sec
en: ~200K writes/sec
~1.25K writes/sec
~50K writes/sec
~12.5K writes/sec

why.hi: 50K / 4 = 12.5K/sec sirf ek city. Isliye latest location Redis GEO me overwrite, DB me har update nahi.
why.en: 50K / 4 = 12.5K/sec for one city. So overwrite the latest location in Redis GEO, not the DB on every update.

q.hi: Uber ne geohash precision 6 pe sirf user ka apna cell query kiya. Kabhi kabhi 100 m door wala driver nahi dikhta. Kyun?
q.en: Uber queries only the user's own geohash cell at precision 6. Sometimes a driver 100 m away is missed. Why?

hi: User cell ke edge pe hai aur driver bagal ke cell me; apna cell + 8 neighbours query karna chahiye
Precision 6 bahut chhota hai, 150 m cell hota hai
Geohash sirf static places ke liye kaam karta hai
B-tree index geohash strings pe kaam nahi karta
en: The user is at a cell edge and the driver is in the next cell; query own cell + 8 neighbours
Precision 6 is too small, cells are 150 m
Geohash only works for static places
A B-tree index does not work on geohash strings

why.hi: Common prefix = paas paas, par ulta hamesha sach nahi. 9 cells fetch karke exact distance se filter aur sort.
why.en: Common prefix means nearby, but nearby does not always share a prefix. Fetch 9 cells, then filter and sort by exact distance.

q.hi: Moving drivers ke liye in-memory quadtree kyun kam suitable hai?
q.en: Why is an in-memory quadtree less suitable for moving drivers?

hi: Quadtree dense areas me bade cells banata hai
Frequent updates pe tree split/rebalance mehenga hai; quadtree static places ke liye best hai
Quadtree radius query support hi nahi karta
Quadtree ko PostGIS ke bina chala hi nahi sakte
en: A quadtree creates large cells in dense areas
Frequent updates make tree splits/rebalancing expensive; quadtrees suit static places
A quadtree cannot answer radius queries at all
A quadtree cannot run without PostGIS

why.hi: Quadtree dense area me chhote cells banata hai (achha), par moving objects ke liye Redis GEO behtar hai.
why.en: A quadtree uses small cells in dense areas (good), but Redis GEO is better for moving objects.

q.hi: Inverted index: paneer → [3, 7, 19, 42], tikka → [7, 11, 42]. Query "paneer tikka" (AND) ka result?
q.en: Inverted index: paneer → [3, 7, 19, 42], tikka → [7, 11, 42]. Result of query "paneer tikka" (AND)?

why.hi: AND query = posting lists ka intersection. Lists sorted hoti hain, isliye intersection fast.
why.en: An AND query is the intersection of posting lists. The lists are sorted, so intersection is fast.

q.hi: BookMyShow events Postgres me hain aur search Elasticsearch me. DB → ES sync ka best tareeka?
q.en: BookMyShow events live in Postgres and search in Elasticsearch. Best way to sync DB → ES?

hi: Dual write: app DB aur ES dono me likhe
Har 10 min updated_at > last_run wala batch job
ES ko hi source of truth bana do, Postgres hata do
CDC: Debezium binlog/WAL padhe → Kafka → idempotent indexer → ES
en: Dual write: the app writes to both DB and ES
A batch job every 10 min on updated_at > last_run
Make ES the source of truth and drop Postgres
CDC: Debezium reads the binlog/WAL → Kafka → idempotent indexer → ES

why.hi: Dual write partial failure pe out of sync karta hai; batch stale hai aur deletes miss karta hai. CDC reliable aur ordered.
why.en: Dual writes drift on partial failure; batch is stale and misses deletes. CDC is reliable and ordered.

q.hi: Typeahead trie bada hai aur "pa" ka subtree huge. Har keystroke pe fast suggestions kaise?
q.en: The typeahead trie is large and the "pa" subtree is huge. How do you return suggestions fast on every keystroke?

hi: Har node pe top-K suggestions precompute karo, aur trie offline batch se rebuild karke swap karo
Har query pe poora subtree traverse karke sort karo
Har keystroke pe trie frequencies real-time update karo
SQL LIKE 'pa%' query chalao
en: Precompute top-K suggestions at every node and rebuild the trie offline in batch, then swap
Traverse and sort the whole subtree on every query
Update trie frequencies in real time on every keystroke
Run a SQL LIKE 'pa%' query

why.hi: Precomputed top-K se lookup O(prefix length). Updates search logs → Kafka → hourly/daily batch.
why.en: With precomputed top-K, lookup is O(prefix length). Updates flow from search logs → Kafka → hourly/daily batch.

q.hi: Hotstar ko roz ke unique viewers (crore me) count karne hain, ~1% error chalega. Best structure?
q.en: Hotstar needs daily unique viewers (in crores); ~1% error is fine. Best structure?

hi: Redis SET of all user IDs
HyperLogLog (~12 KB, ~0.81% error)
Count-Min Sketch
Bloom filter
en: A Redis SET of all user IDs
HyperLogLog (~12 KB, ~0.81% error)
Count-Min Sketch
Bloom filter

why.hi: HLL cardinality deta hai fixed 12 KB me. Exact set me 1 crore IDs ~100s MB. CMS frequency batata hai, unique count nahi.
why.en: HLL estimates cardinality in a fixed 12 KB. An exact set of 1 crore IDs is ~100s of MB. CMS gives frequency, not uniques.

q.hi: Trending hashtags ke liye Count-Min Sketch use kiya. Iska error kis type ka hota hai?
q.en: You use a Count-Min Sketch for trending hashtags. What kind of error does it have?

hi: Sirf under-estimate
Dono taraf random error
Sirf over-estimate: count kabhi kam nahi aata, thoda zyada aa sakta hai
False negatives, item dikhta hi nahi
en: Only under-estimates
Random error in both directions
Only over-estimates: counts are never too low, possibly a bit high
False negatives, the item is not found at all

why.hi: Query pe saari rows ka minimum lete hain; collisions sirf counters badhate hain, isliye over-estimate.
why.en: The query takes the minimum across rows; collisions only add to counters, so it over-estimates.

q.hi: Har shard apna local top-10 nikalta hai aur aggregator merge karta hai. Global top-10 galat kyun aa sakta hai, aur fix?
q.en: Each shard computes a local top-10 and an aggregator merges them. Why can the global top-10 be wrong, and the fix?

hi: Min-heap size K galat hai, max-heap use karo
Aggregator ko HyperLogLog use karna chahiye
Shards ko tumbling window ki jagah session window chahiye
Koi item har shard pe 11th ho sakta hai par total me top; key se partition karo taaki ek item ka poora count ek shard pe ho
en: The size-K min-heap is wrong; use a max-heap
The aggregator should use HyperLogLog
Shards need session windows instead of tumbling windows
An item can be 11th on every shard yet top overall; partition by key so each item's full count lives on one shard

why.hi: Local top-K merge exact tabhi hai jab ek item ka count ek hi shard pe ho (Kafka me key-based partitioning).
why.en: Merging local top-K is exact only when each item's count is on one shard (key-based partitioning in Kafka).

q.hi: Swiggy order: Order, Payment, Inventory teen alag services aur DBs. Interview me default approach?
q.en: Swiggy order: Order, Payment and Inventory are separate services and DBs. Default approach in an interview?

hi: Saga (critical flow ke liye orchestrated), har step ka compensating action jaise refund
2PC across all services
Ek global BEGIN ... COMMIT
Teeno services ek hi DB share karein bina boundaries ke
en: Saga (orchestrated for critical flows), with a compensating action per step such as a refund
2PC across all services
A single global BEGIN ... COMMIT
Have all three services share one DB without boundaries

why.hi: 2PC blocking hai aur payment gateway/Kafka usme participate nahi karte. Saga local transactions + compensation.
why.en: 2PC blocks, and payment gateways/Kafka cannot participate. Saga uses local transactions + compensation.

q.hi: Order Service DB me order commit karta hai, phir Kafka publish se pehle crash. Event kho gaya. Fix?
q.en: Order Service commits the order to the DB, then crashes before publishing to Kafka. The event is lost. Fix?

hi: Pehle Kafka publish, phir DB commit
Transactional outbox: event same DB transaction me outbox table me likho, CDC/relay Kafka me daale
Kafka exactly-once enable kar do, bas
Publish fail ho to 5 sec baad app se retry
en: Publish to Kafka first, then commit to the DB
Transactional outbox: write the event to an outbox table in the same DB transaction; CDC/relay publishes to Kafka
Just enable Kafka exactly-once
Retry the publish from the app after 5 seconds

why.hi: Ye dual write problem hai. Outbox se DB commit hua to event zaroor jayega (at-least-once); consumers idempotent rakho.
why.en: This is the dual-write problem. With an outbox, a committed DB write always yields the event (at-least-once); keep consumers idempotent.

q.hi: 2PC me coordinator prepare phase ke baad crash ho gaya. Participants ka kya hota hai?
q.en: In 2PC the coordinator crashes after the prepare phase. What happens to the participants?

hi: Sab automatically commit kar dete hain
Sab automatically abort karke compensation chalate hain
Woh locks pakde wait karte rehte hain (blocking) jab tak coordinator wapas na aaye
Sabse fast participant naya coordinator ban ke commit karta hai
en: They all commit automatically
They all abort automatically and run compensations
They wait holding locks (blocking) until the coordinator returns
The fastest participant becomes coordinator and commits

why.hi: Isi blocking, slowness aur kam availability ki wajah se microservices me 2PC avoid karte hain.
why.en: This blocking, slowness and reduced availability is why 2PC is avoided in microservices.

q.hi: Snowflake ID (1 + 41 + 10 + 12 bits) me ek machine ek millisecond me max kitni IDs bana sakti hai?
q.en: In a Snowflake ID (1 + 41 + 10 + 12 bits), how many IDs can one machine generate per millisecond?

why.hi: 12-bit sequence = 2^12 = 4096 per ms, yaani ~4M IDs/sec per machine. 10 bit machine ID = 1024 machines.
why.en: The 12-bit sequence gives 2^12 = 4096 per ms, about 4M IDs/sec per machine. The 10-bit machine ID allows 1024 machines.

q.hi: High-write table me UUID v4 primary key hai aur inserts slow ho rahe hain. Kyun, aur better option?
q.en: A high-write table uses UUID v4 as primary key and inserts are slowing down. Why, and a better option?

hi: Random IDs B-tree me page splits karte hain; time-ordered UUID v7 / Snowflake end pe append karte hain
UUID v4 me collision bahut hote hain; auto-increment lo
UUID v4 64 bit hai, isliye chhota padta hai; 128 bit lo
UUID v4 ko generate karne ke liye central server chahiye
en: Random IDs cause B-tree page splits; time-ordered UUID v7 / Snowflake append at the end
UUID v4 collides often; use auto-increment
UUID v4 is 64 bits and too small; use 128 bits
UUID v4 needs a central server to generate

why.hi: v4 ka collision practically impossible hai (2^122), problem index write performance hai. v7 me pehle 48 bit timestamp.
why.en: v4 collisions are practically impossible (2^122); the problem is index write performance. v7 starts with a 48-bit timestamp.

q.hi: Snowflake generator wali machine pe NTP ne clock 2 sec peeche kar di. Kya risk hai aur kya karna chahiye?
q.en: NTP moved the clock 2 seconds back on a Snowflake generator machine. What is the risk and what should it do?

hi: IDs 128 bit ho jaayengi
Duplicate IDs ban sakti hain; clock peeche jaaye to wait karo ya error do
Machine ID badal jayega
Koi risk nahi, sequence bits handle kar lete hain
en: IDs will become 128 bits
Duplicate IDs may be generated; wait or return an error when the clock goes backwards
The machine ID will change
No risk, the sequence bits handle it

why.hi: Same timestamp + machine + sequence dobara aa sakta hai. Snowflake me collision tabhi nahi jab machine ID unique ho aur clock peeche na jaaye.
why.en: The same timestamp + machine + sequence can repeat. Snowflake is collision-free only with unique machine IDs and a clock that never goes back.

q.hi: Instagram feed: normal users push se, par Virat Kohli (27 crore followers) ki post ka kya karein?
q.en: Instagram feed: normal users use push, but what about a post by Virat Kohli (27 crore followers)?

hi: Sab 27 crore timelines me synchronously push karo
Poore system ko pull pe shift kar do
Hybrid: celebrity posts push mat karo, feed read time pe pull karke merge karo
Celebrity posts sirf active followers ko hi dikhao, baaki ko kabhi nahi
en: Push synchronously into all 27 crore timelines
Move the whole system to pull
Hybrid: do not push celebrity posts; pull and merge them at feed read time
Show celebrity posts only to active followers and never to others

why.hi: Push celebrity ke liye crore writes aur queue block karta hai. Pull sabke liye read mehenga karta hai. Hybrid dono ka best.
why.en: Push means crores of writes and a blocked queue for celebrities. Pull everywhere makes reads costly. Hybrid takes the best of both.

q.hi: 200M DAU, har user ~2 posts/day, average 200 followers, sab push. Approx timeline writes/sec?
q.en: 200M DAU, ~2 posts/user/day, 200 followers on average, all push. Approximate timeline writes/sec?

hi: ~4,600 writes/sec
~100K writes/sec
~10M writes/sec
~1M writes/sec (80B/day)
en: ~4,600 writes/sec
~100K writes/sec
~10M writes/sec
~1M writes/sec (80B/day)

why.hi: 400M posts x 200 = 80B/day, / 10^5 sec ≈ 800K-1M/sec. 4,600/sec sirf posts/sec hai, writes nahi.
why.en: 400M posts x 200 = 80B/day, / 10^5 sec ≈ 800K-1M/sec. 4,600/sec is just posts/sec, not writes.

q.hi: Redis timeline cache timeline:{userId} me kya store karna chahiye?
q.en: What should be stored in the Redis timeline cache timeline:{userId}?

hi: Sirf post IDs, LPUSH + LTRIM se latest ~800
Poora post object (text, media URL, likes)
User ke saare posts ever, bina limit ke
Followers ki list
en: Only post IDs, kept to the latest ~800 with LPUSH + LTRIM
The full post object (text, media URL, likes)
Every post ever, with no limit
The list of followers

why.hi: 8 B x 800 ≈ 6.4 KB/user; 100M users ≈ 640 GB. Post content alag cache se aata hai; bina LTRIM memory phat jaati hai.
why.en: 8 B x 800 ≈ 6.4 KB/user; 100M users ≈ 640 GB. Post content comes from a separate cache; without LTRIM memory blows up.

q.hi: In HTTP methods me se kaunsa idempotent NAHI hai?
q.en: Which of these HTTP methods is NOT idempotent?

hi: PUT
POST
DELETE
GET
en: PUT
POST
DELETE
GET

why.hi: POST create/action hai; payment jaise POST ko Idempotency-Key header se idempotent banao.
why.en: POST creates/acts; make POSTs like payments idempotent with an Idempotency-Key header.

q.hi: Instagram jaisi infinite scroll feed ke liye pagination?
q.en: Pagination for an Instagram-style infinite scroll feed?

hi: Offset: LIMIT 20 OFFSET n
Page number + total count har request pe
Cursor: WHERE id < last_id ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 20, opaque next_cursor ke saath
Poori feed ek response me, client paginate kare
en: Offset: LIMIT 20 OFFSET n
Page number + total count on every request
Cursor: WHERE id < last_id ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 20, with an opaque next_cursor
The whole feed in one response; the client paginates

why.hi: Offset deep pages pe slow (rows skip) aur naye posts aane pe duplicates/skips deta hai. Cursor index seek se hamesha fast.
why.en: Offset is slow on deep pages (skipping rows) and duplicates/skips when new posts arrive. Cursor uses an index seek and stays fast.

q.hi: Report generate karne me ~2 min lagte hain. API kaise design karoge?
q.en: Generating a report takes ~2 minutes. How would you design the API?

hi: 200 OK, request 2 min tak open rakho
201 Created turant, khaali report ke saath
Client 2 min ka timeout rakhe aur fail pe retry kare
202 Accepted + jobId (Location: /jobs/77), client poll kare ya webhook/SSE se notify
en: 200 OK, keep the request open for 2 minutes
201 Created immediately with an empty report
Client sets a 2-min timeout and retries on failure
202 Accepted + jobId (Location: /jobs/77); the client polls or gets notified via webhook/SSE

why.hi: Lamba kaam synchronous rakha to timeout pe client retry karega aur kaam double hoga. Status: QUEUED → RUNNING → DONE/FAILED.
why.en: Keeping long work synchronous means timeouts, client retries and duplicate work. Status: QUEUED → RUNNING → DONE/FAILED.

q.hi: 99.9% availability ka matlab saal me roughly kitna downtime allowed hai?
q.en: Roughly how much yearly downtime does 99.9% availability allow?

hi: ~8.8 ghante
~52 min
~5 min
en: ~8.8 hours
~52 minutes
~3.65 days
~5 minutes

q.hi: Circuit breaker OPEN state me hai aur 30 sec cooldown khatam hua. Ab kya hota hai?
q.en: A circuit breaker is OPEN and its 30-sec cooldown ends. What happens next?

hi: Seedha CLOSED, saara traffic wapas
HALF-OPEN: kuch test calls jaati hain; success pe CLOSED, fail pe wapas OPEN
Permanent OPEN jab tak manual reset na ho
Saari pending requests ek saath retry hoti hain
en: Straight to CLOSED with all traffic restored
HALF-OPEN: a few test calls go through; success → CLOSED, failure → back to OPEN
Stays OPEN permanently until manually reset
All pending requests are retried at once

why.hi: OPEN me fail fast + fallback (cached/default). HALF-OPEN dheere se recovery check karta hai.
why.en: OPEN fails fast with a fallback (cached/default). HALF-OPEN carefully probes for recovery.

q.hi: Team bolti hai: "Hamare paas 3 replicas hain, backup ki zarurat nahi." Kya galat hai?
q.en: The team says: "We have 3 replicas, so we do not need backups." What is wrong?

hi: Kuch nahi, 3 replicas = backup
Replicas async hain isliye sirf RTO badhta hai
Galat DELETE ya corruption replicas pe bhi replicate hota hai; snapshot + WAL archive se point-in-time recovery chahiye
Backup sirf multi-region setup me chahiye
en: Nothing, 3 replicas are a backup
Replicas are async, so only RTO increases
A bad DELETE or corruption replicates too; you need snapshots + WAL archive for point-in-time recovery
Backups are only needed in multi-region setups

why.hi: Replication availability deti hai, backup nahi. Backups doosre region me rakho aur restore practice karo.
why.en: Replication gives availability, not backups. Keep backups in another region and practise restores.

q.hi: 100M requests/day ka average QPS roughly kitna hai (1 din ≈ 10^5 sec)?
q.en: Roughly what is the average QPS of 100M requests/day (1 day ≈ 10^5 sec)?

hi: ~100 QPS
en: ~100 QPS

why.hi: 10^8 / 10^5 = 10^3. Peak normally 2-5x, IPL/flash sale pe 10x+.
why.en: 10^8 / 10^5 = 10^3. Peak is usually 2-5x, and 10x+ for IPL/flash sales.

q.hi: Inme se kaunsa sabse SLOW hai?
q.en: Which of these is the SLOWEST?

hi: HDD disk seek (~10 ms)
SSD random read (~100 µs)
Same datacenter round trip (~0.5 ms)
Main memory read (~100 ns)
en: HDD disk seek (~10 ms)
SSD random read (~100 µs)
Same-datacenter round trip (~0.5 ms)
Main memory read (~100 ns)

why.hi: RAM (100 ns) < SSD (100 µs) < same-DC network (0.5 ms) < HDD seek (10 ms). Cross-continent 150 ms+ isse bhi slow.
why.en: RAM (100 ns) < SSD (100 µs) < same-DC network (0.5 ms) < HDD seek (10 ms). Cross-continent at 150 ms+ is slower still.

q.hi: Photo app: 10M uploads/day, average photo 500 KB. Yearly storage roughly kitna (replication ke bina)?
q.en: Photo app: 10M uploads/day, 500 KB per photo. Roughly how much storage per year (before replication)?

hi: ~5 TB/year
~1.8 PB/year
~180 TB/year
~18 PB/year
en: ~5 TB/year
~1.8 PB/year
~180 TB/year
~18 PB/year

why.hi: 10M x 500 KB = 5 TB/day, x 365 ≈ 1.8 PB. Isliye photos blob storage me; replication 3x bhi jodna mat bhoolo.
why.en: 10M x 500 KB = 5 TB/day, x 365 ≈ 1.8 PB. Hence blob storage; and remember to add 3x for replication.

q.hi: Candidate bolta hai "Yahan Cassandra lagayenge" aur aage badh jaata hai. Isko strong answer kaise banaye?
q.en: A candidate says "We will put Cassandra here" and moves on. How to make it a strong answer?

hi: Saath me Kafka, Redis aur Kubernetes bhi bol do
Cassandra ka internal architecture 10 min explain karo
"Kyunki" aur "kya nahi chuna" jodo: write-heavy hai, multi-row txn nahi chahiye; Postgres nahi kyunki 1M writes/sec ek node pe nahi hoga
Interviewer ke "kyun?" poochhne ka wait karo
en: Also mention Kafka, Redis and Kubernetes
Explain Cassandra's internals for 10 minutes
Add a "because" and "what I did not pick": write-heavy, no multi-row txns; not Postgres because 1M writes/sec will not fit on one node
Wait for the interviewer to ask "why?"

why.hi: Tech naam bina justification buzzword hai. Har choice ke saath trade-off bolna green flag hai.
why.en: A tech name without justification is a buzzword. Stating the trade-off with every choice is a green flag.

q.hi: Tumne pure push fan-out design kiya. Interviewer poochhta hai "Agar ek celebrity ke 10M followers ho to?" Best response?
q.en: You designed pure push fan-out. The interviewer asks "What if a celebrity has 10M followers?" Best response?

hi: Defend karo ki push hi sahi hai, Kafka sab sambhal lega
Bolo ki celebrities scope me nahi the aur aage badho
Poora design mita ke shuru se pull pe banao
Ise hint maano: "Achha point hai", problem accept karo aur hybrid fan-out ki taraf design evolve karo
en: Defend that push is right and Kafka will handle it
Say celebrities were out of scope and move on
Erase the design and rebuild everything as pull
Treat it as a hint: "Good point", accept the problem and evolve the design toward hybrid fan-out

why.hi: Interviewer ka hint usually sahi direction hai. Behes karna ya ignore karna collaboration ka bura signal hai.
why.en: The interviewer's hint usually points the right way. Arguing or ignoring it signals poor collaboration.

q.hi: Requirement 1,000 QPS ki hai. Candidate 12 microservices, multi-region active-active aur service mesh propose karta hai. Kya red flag hai?
q.en: The requirement is 1,000 QPS. A candidate proposes 12 microservices, multi-region active-active and a service mesh. What is the red flag?

hi: Over-engineering: simple design se shuru karo, phir batao 10x scale pe kya badlega
Deep dive na karna
Zarurat se zyada estimation
